reviewer.subagents: Three subagents drafted X01–X29, X30–X58 and V01–V33 respectively. The lead reviewer drafted V34–V66. The four groups were assigned to different reviewers for the adversarial pass, and the lead reviewer assembled and validated the comparison.

segments.sense: The heading announces an exact and clear compendium of music.

best_ru.why: The Russian heading is compact and idiomatic.

best_en.why: All retain the announcement, accuracy, clarity, and summary.

segments.sense: The ancients maintained that music holds this universe together. Nothing in nature exists without due measure and proportion. The argument continues in X03.

text_issues_review.printed: VNiuersum hoc, antiqui Musica / contineri perhibuerunt. Nihil e- / nim in rerum natura absque com- / mensuratione et proportione con- / sistit: neque quicquam eorum quæ
text_issues_review.proposal: Эта вселенная, как утверждали древние, заключена в музыке. / This universe, the ancients declared, is contained in music.
text_issues_review.why: A bare ablative with contineor can be locative, as Allen and Greenough §431 specifically notes, so the grammar alone does not rule out ‘contained within music’. Here the following claim that due measure and proportion operate throughout nature and X07's account of music arranging all things support the stronger causal ‘held together by music’.
evidence: Allen and Greenough, New Latin Grammar, §§409 and 431 [checked]
Lewis and Short, A Latin Dictionary, s.v. contineo A [checked]
Boethius, De institutione musica I.2, ed. Friedlein (1867), pp. 187–189 [checked]

best_ru.why: The active construction conveys what holds the universe together.

best_en.why: Both preserve the cosmic claim and the two distinct measure terms.

notes_to_keep.gist: Explain the sense of commensuratio and its coordination with proportio and proportionalitas.
Boethius, De institutione musica I.2, ed. Friedlein (1867), pp. 187–189 [checked] gives a precise parallel for cosmic music in the heavens, elements, and seasons.

segments.sense: Nothing that comes about without due measure and proportion is said to have been properly produced or born, whether art or nature brings it about and whether sense or intellect alone apprehends it.

errors.quote: anything among the things that come to be said to have been
errors.problem: The uninterrupted words invite a reading in which come to be governs said. The Latin separates quae fiunt from the main dicitur.
errors.fix: Set the condition off before the main predicate, as in C.

best_ru.why: The conditional and both pairs are clear.

best_en.why: Both keep the condition and the two independent pairs of alternatives.

segments.sense: Music itself, considered in itself, is assuredly a kind of due measure and proportionality, being the harmony of the universe.

divergences.latin: commensuratio quaedam omnino et proportionalitas est
divergences.issue: Does omnino mark extent or reinforce the assertion?

readings.construal: Extent, as all-round or complete measure.

quotes.ru: Музыка же сама по себе есть всецело некая соразмерность и пропорциональность, будучи, разумеется, гармонией вселенной.
quotes.en: Music itself, moreover, is in its own right altogether a certain commensuration and proportionality, being, to be sure, the harmony of the universe.

quotes.ru: Музыка же сама по себе есть всецело некая соразмерность и пропорциональность: она, разумеется, и есть гармония вселенной.
quotes.en: Now music itself is in itself altogether a kind of commensuration and proportionality, being, indeed, the harmony of the universe.

readings.construal: Emphatic assertion that music is a kind of due measure and proportionality.

quotes.ru: Сама же музыка по себе, несомненно, есть своего рода соразмерность и пропорциональность, ибо она представляет собой гармонию вселенной.
quotes.en: Music in itself is assuredly a kind of commensurateness and proportionality, for it is the harmony of the universe.

quotes.ru: Сама же музыка есть, без сомнения, некая соразмерность и пропорциональность, ибо она и есть гармония вселенной.
quotes.en: Music in itself is certainly a kind of commensuration and proportionality, being, of course, the harmony of the universe.

divergences.verdict: Both adverbial effects are possible. Emphasis on the assertion is clearer with quaedam, an indefinite qualification that remains operative.
divergences.recommended_ru: Музыка сама по себе, несомненно, есть своего рода соразмерность и пропорциональность.
divergences.recommended_en: Music in itself is indeed a kind of due measure and proportionality.
evidence: Lewis & Short, s.v. omnino I and II.B [checked]

errors.quote: Сама же музыка есть, без сомнения
errors.problem: ‘Сама’ conveys ipsa, but the separate per se qualification, explicitly retained in D's English, has no Russian equivalent.
errors.fix: Use «Сама же музыка, взятая сама по себе, несомненно, есть…» or the less repetitive «Музыка же сама по себе несомненно есть…».

text_issues_review.printed: Cæterùm Musica ipsa per se commensura- / tio quædam omnino et proportionalitas est, ni- / mirum harmonia uniuersi existens. Fortassis et
text_issues_review.proposal: Сама музыка по себе во всех отношениях есть своего рода соразмерность и пропорциональность. / Music itself is in every respect a kind of commensurateness and proportionality.
text_issues_review.why: The general intensive sense supports the alternative's extent. The indefinite quaedam and the definition together favor the assertion-level reading, which is also a way to render the intensive without making a claim about separate respects.
evidence: Lewis and Short, A Latin Dictionary, s.v. omnino I [checked]

best_ru.why: Gives per se and allows omnino to reinforce the assertion.

best_en.why: Keeps in itself, both measure terms, and the explanatory participle.

notes_to_keep.gist: Preserve the change from proportio to proportionalitas. The Boethian technical distinction concerns a relation of terms and the correspondence of ratios. Boethius, De institutione musica II.12–14, ed. Friedlein (1867), pp. 242–244 [checked]

editor_questions: Choose the force of omnino in the main assertion. Keep the distinct forms proportio and proportionalitas visible across X02–X04.

segments.sense: One might aptly even call divine nature itself the harmony of itself and the universe, since the world, ordered in God and fitted for consonance, seems to be in the best possible state.

errors.quote: явно пребывает
errors.problem: The formulation substitutes explicit certainty for the appearance expressed by videtur.
errors.fix: по-видимому, пребывает

best_ru.why: Preserves the qualification and the emphatic superlative.

best_en.why: Both make the tentative comparison and the progression from well to as well as possible explicit.

notes_to_keep.gist: Retain the distinction between concinnare and coaptare and trace the musical force of consonantia back into the cosmological claim.

segments.sense: The greatness of the wonder the ancients accorded music follows from what has just been said.

best_ru.why: Makes the anaphoric subject clear and conveys the ancients' judgment.

best_en.why: Convey dignari without a misleading suggestion of supernatural events.

notes_to_keep.gist: Link the sense of miraculum to Pliny's tree worthy of wonder, and identify illi as the ancients of X02. Lewis and Short, s.v. miraculum I and dignor [checked].

segments.sense: Music is discernible in all things, regulates and adorns them all, and gives pleasure to sense, accord (that is, harmony) to nature, and blessedness to intellect. The author will briefly discuss music considered in the senses, strictly in hearing.

divergences.latin: quae in sensibus, aut potius uno sensuum auditu consideratur
divergences.issue: Is the final relative clause about music as an object of consideration or direct perception?

readings.construal: Music considered by or in the domain of the senses, more precisely by hearing.

quotes.ru: Поскольку она усматривается во всём, всё упорядочивает и украшает и к тому же дарует чувству наслаждение, природе — согласованность (я разумею гармонию), а уму, наконец, — блаженство, мы кратко скажем о той музыке, которая рассматривается в чувствах, или, вернее, в одном из чувств — слухе.
quotes.en: Since it is seen in all things, and tempers and adorns the whole, and moreover bestows pleasure on sense, congruence (I mean harmony) on Nature, and lastly blessedness on the intellect, we shall discourse briefly of that Music which is considered in the senses, or rather in one of the senses, hearing.

quotes.ru: Музыка обнаруживается во всём, всё соразмеряет и украшает, доставляет чувству удовольствие, природе — согласованность (я имею в виду гармонию), а разуму — блаженство. Поэтому мы вкратце поговорим о музыке, которую рассматривают посредством чувств, вернее, одного из них — слуха.
quotes.en: Since music is discernible in all things, tempers and adorns them all, and grants pleasure to sense, accord (I mean harmony) to nature, and finally blessedness to the intellect, we shall speak briefly of music as considered by the senses, or rather by one of them, hearing.

quotes.ru: Поскольку она усматривается во всём, всё умеряет и украшает и дарует чувству наслаждение, природе — согласованность (я разумею гармонию), а уму, наконец, — блаженство, мы вкратце поведём речь о той музыке, которая рассматривается в чувствах, или, вернее, в одном из чувств — в слухе.
quotes.en: Since it is seen in all things, and tempers and adorns all things, and bestows pleasure on sense, congruence (I mean harmony) on Nature, and finally blessedness on the intellect, we shall discuss briefly that music which is considered in the senses, or rather in the one sense of hearing.

readings.construal: Music directly perceived by the senses, more precisely by hearing.

quotes.ru: Поскольку музыка обнаруживается во всём, всему даёт строй и всё украшает, а также дарует чувству удовольствие, природе — согласие (я разумею гармонию), а уму, наконец, — блаженство, мы вкратце скажем о той музыке, которую воспринимают чувствами, вернее, одним из чувств — слухом.
quotes.en: Since music is discernible in all things, brings all things into due order and adorns them, and gives pleasure to sense, agreement (I mean harmony) to nature and, finally, blessedness to the intellect, we shall speak briefly of the music that is perceived by the senses, or, more precisely, by one of them, hearing.

divergences.verdict: Both concern the auditory domain. Consideratur favors examination or consideration, in keeping with disseremus, and retains a verbal distinction from conspicitur at the beginning.
divergences.recommended_ru: о той музыке, которую рассматривают посредством чувств — точнее, посредством одного из них, слуха
divergences.recommended_en: of music as considered through the senses, or more precisely through one of them, hearing
evidence: Lewis and Short, A Latin Dictionary, s.v. considero I–II [checked]
Boethius, De institutione musica I.2, ed. Friedlein (1867), pp. 187–189 [checked]

errors.quote: A threefold division: music of sense, of nature and of the intellect
errors.problem: The single subject music confers three gifts on three recipients. The clause does not divide music into those three classes as Boethius expressly does with his different criteria in I.2.
errors.fix: Distinguish the three effects and the narrower auditory subject of the ensuing exposition.

errors.quote: music that is perceived by the senses / музыку, которую воспринимают чувствами
errors.problem: Consideratur introduces the domain in which the author will examine music. Direct perception shifts the focus away from considering music under its auditory aspect.
errors.fix: Use ‘music as considered in the domain of sense, more precisely of hearing’ / «музыка, рассматриваемая в области чувственного восприятия, точнее слуха».

best_ru.why: Makes the audible domain explicit while keeping the methodological verb.

best_en.why: Preserves the progression from the general scope of music to the faculty that considers it.

notes_to_keep.gist: Keep the lexical note on beatitas and Vinet's beatitudo, subject to verification of any claim of first coinage.
Music brings things into proper measure and Xylander glosses congruentia with harmonia.

segments.sense: A musical note is the pitch-tension, or sustained tone, of voice undivided by any interval and capable of entering harmony.

divergences.issue: How does the doublet define a note?

readings.construal: Tension and actual holding of the voice.

quotes.ru: Звук есть причастное гармонии напряжение, или удержание, голоса, не разделённого никаким интервалом.
quotes.en: A note is a tension, or sustained holding, of a voice divided by no interval, [a tension] that partakes of harmony.

readings.construal: Tension and pitch of the voice.

quotes.ru: Звук есть причастное гармонии напряжение, или высота, голоса, не разделённого никаким интервалом.
quotes.en: A note is the tension, or pitch, of a voice undivided by any interval, [a tension] partaking of harmony.

readings.construal: Pitch and its steady or sustained sounding.

quotes.ru: Звук — это высота, или выдерживаемый тон, голосового звучания, не разделённого никаким интервалом, причём эта высота причастна гармонии.
quotes.en: A note is a pitch, or sustained tone, of vocal sound undivided by any interval, a pitch that partakes of harmony.

quotes.ru: Звук — это высота голоса, не разделённого никаким интервалом, иначе говоря, его ровное звучание, причастное гармонии.
quotes.en: A note is the pitch, or steady tone, of a voice undivided by any interval, a pitch that partakes of harmony.

divergences.verdict: Boethius places the voice on one intensio, supporting pitch as the value of the term here. Tenor can mean holding or tone. Sustained tone captures both strands without implying strain or emphasizing duration above constancy of pitch.
divergences.recommended_ru: высота, или выдерживаемый тон, голоса
divergences.recommended_en: the pitch, or sustained tone, of the voice
evidence: Lewis and Short, A Latin Dictionary, s.v. tenor I (Quintilian 1.5.22, 26) [checked]
Boethius, De institutione musica I.8, ed. Friedlein (1867), p. 195 [checked]

text_issues_review.printed: Sonus est, uocis nullo interuallo diuisæ har- / moniæ particeps intensio, seu tenor. Interuallum
text_issues_review.proposal: Звук есть напряжение, или удержание, голоса, причастное гармонии, не разделённой никаким интервалом. / A note is a tension, or sustained holding, of the voice that partakes of a harmony divided by no interval.
text_issues_review.why: Genitive divisae can formally agree with either noun. X12 immediately expounds indivisibility as a property of the note and separately expounds participation in harmony. The grammar and that sequence favor divisae with vocis.
evidence: Boethius, De institutione musica I.8, ed. Friedlein (1867), p. 195 [checked]

text_issues_review.printed: Sonus est, uocis nullo interuallo diuisæ har- / moniæ particeps intensio, seu tenor. Interuallum
text_issues_review.proposal: Звук — причастная гармонии высота, или устойчивый уровень высоты, голосового звучания, не разделённого никаким интервалом. / A note is a pitch, or steady level of pitch, of vocal sound undivided by any interval, which participates in harmony.
text_issues_review.why: Steady level of pitch is supported by tenor in Quintilian and by the reference to a single pitch. The supplied alternative's final English relative clause needs recasting so that particeps qualifies the pitch, the head of the Latin definition.
evidence: Lewis and Short, A Latin Dictionary, s.v. tenor I (Quintilian 1.5.22, 26) [checked]
Boethius, De institutione musica I.8, ed. Friedlein (1867), p. 195 [checked]

best_en.why: Distinguish pitch from its sustained-tone gloss and avoid ambiguity about what partakes of harmony.

notes_to_keep.gist: Keep Boethius's definition by one pitch suitable for melody. Boethius, De institutione musica I.8, ed. Friedlein (1867), p. 195 [checked]

best_ru.why: Renders the relative ordering and the doublet naturally.

segments.sense: A system is a definite combination of intervals.

text_issues_review.printed: siue respectus. Systema, complexus est certus / interuallorum. Harmonia, ipsa constructio sy-
text_issues_review.proposal: Система — некое сочетание интервалов. / A system is a certain combination of intervals.

best_en.why: All distinguish a definite configuration of intervals.

best_ru.why: The four Russian versions coincide.

segments.sense: A note cannot be divided, like a point in geometry. It is said to partake of harmony because it can be sounded so as to fit with another note to form harmony.

best_ru.why: Clearly distinguishes the analogy and the reason for harmony participation.

best_en.why: Give idiomatic expression to the capacity to be fitted to another note.

segments.sense: If this does not occur, the sound is dissonant rather than consonant. It is then classed as randomly produced noise that is of no use for consonance.

segments.sense: Xylander says that a sixteen-string arrangement is realized on an instrument actually equipped with fifteen strings. The end of the first octachord serves immediately as the beginning of the following series. Two eight-note spans therefore share one position, giving 8 + 8 − 1 = 15.

divergences.latin: heccaedecachordum … in quindecim fidibus instructo organo … absolvitur
divergences.issue: How is the sixteen-string entity related to the instrument of fifteen strings?

readings.construal: A named sixteen-string entity is realized on the physically fifteen-string instrument, with both names retained as Greek-derived forms.

quotes.ru: Этими видами звуков геккайдекахорд, то есть инструмент о шестнадцати струнах, осуществляется на инструменте, снабжённом пятнадцатью струнами (греки называют его пентекайдекахордом), поскольку конец октахорда тотчас принимается за начало последующих.
quotes.en: Through these species of notes the hekkaidekachord, that is, the instrument of sixteen strings, is completed on an instrument furnished with fifteen strings (the Greeks call it a pentekaidekachord), the end of the octachord being taken up directly as the beginning of those that follow.

quotes.ru: Посредством этих видов звуков геккайдекахорд, то есть инструмент из шестнадцати струн, осуществляется на инструменте, снабжённом пятнадцатью струнами (греки называют его пентекайдекахордом): конец октахорда сразу же принимается за начало последующих [звуков].
quotes.en: Through these species of notes the hekkaidekachord, that is, an instrument of sixteen strings, is completed on an instrument fitted with fifteen strings (the Greeks call it the pentekaidekachord), the end of the octachord being taken immediately as the beginning of the following [notes].

readings.construal: The sixteen-string system, glossed as an instrument, is described as inside another instrument.

quotes.ru: Эти виды звуков образуют шестнадцатиструнную систему, то есть шестнадцатиструнный инструмент в инструменте, снабжённом пятнадцатью струнами (греки называют его пятнадцатиструнником): конец октахорда сразу принимают за начало следующих [звуков].
quotes.en: These kinds of notes complete a sixteen-string system, that is, an instrument of sixteen strings within an instrument equipped with fifteen strings (the Greeks call it a fifteen-string instrument), the end of the octachord being taken immediately as the beginning of the [notes] that follow.

readings.construal: The forms are translated descriptively. The sixteen-string arrangement is realized on a fifteen-string instrument.

quotes.ru: Из этих видов звуков на инструменте с пятнадцатью струнами (греки называют его пятнадцатиструнным) складывается шестнадцатиструнный [инструмент], то есть инструмент с шестнадцатью струнами. При этом конец октахорда непосредственно принимается за начало следующих [звуков].
quotes.en: On an instrument strung with fifteen strings (the Greeks call it the fifteen-stringed instrument), these kinds of notes complete the sixteen-stringed instrument, that is, an instrument of sixteen strings. The end of the octachord is taken straightaway as the beginning of the [notes] that follow.

divergences.verdict: In this context the ablative with in marks the instrument on which the arrangement is completed. The sixteen named positions count the boundary note twice. The enclosure wording can mislead. Describing the compounds is sound if their form is given in the note.
divergences.recommended_ru: На инструменте с пятнадцатью струнами (греки называют его пентекайдекахордом) осуществляется геккайдекахорд, то есть инструмент с шестнадцатью струнами.
divergences.recommended_en: The hekkaidekachord, that is, the instrument of sixteen strings, is realized on an instrument equipped with fifteen strings, which the Greeks call a pentekaidekachord.
evidence: Allen and Greenough, New Latin Grammar §426.3 on the place where, in with ablative [checked]
Boethius, De institutione musica I.24–25, ed. Friedlein (1867), shared boundary and disjunction of tetrachords [checked]

errors.quote: шестнадцатиструнный инструмент в инструменте / an instrument of sixteen strings within an instrument
errors.problem: Within suggests that one physical instrument contains another. The text contrasts the number of places in the arrangement with the number of actual strings on which it is played.
errors.fix: на инструменте … / on an instrument …

Quam enim rationem ha-
text_issues_review.proposal: конец октахорда сразу принимают за начало следующих [октахордов] / the end of the octachord being taken immediately as the beginning of the [octachords] that follow

segments.sense: The first note stands to the eighth in the same ratio as the eighth to the fifteenth. Each ascending span is an octave. The pitch multiplier is 2 in each case, 4 for the whole span. The frequency ratio in the order of the Latin is 1:2 for each span, and the inverse direction applies to string lengths at fixed tension and density.

errors.quote: 1st : 8th = octave, 2:1; 8th : 15th = octave, 2:1; 1st : 15th = 4:1
errors.problem: The checks write the lower note first but label each pair with the conventional higher-over-lower pitch ratio without identifying it as such. In the written order the frequency ratios are 1:2, 1:2 and 1:4. An ideal string-length interpretation would invert those.
errors.fix: State that the ascending pitch multipliers are 2, 2 and 4, and specify the order whenever assigning pitch or string-length ratios.

errors.quote: 1 (proslambanomenos) : 8 (mese) = 8 (mese) : 15 (nete hyperbolaion) = an octave, 2:1 in each case; 1 : 15 = double octave, 4:1
errors.problem: The checks write the lower note first but label each pair with the conventional higher-over-lower pitch ratio without identifying it as such. In the written order the frequency ratios are 1:2, 1:2 and 1:4. An ideal string-length interpretation would invert those.
errors.fix: State that the ascending pitch multipliers are 2, 2 and 4, and specify the order whenever assigning pitch or string-length ratios.

best_en.why: Both keep the ratios and their endpoints clear.

notes_to_keep.gist: Keep the distinction between an ascending pitch multiplier and a frequency ratio written in the order of the Latin terms.

best_ru.why: Both give the brief conventional transition.

best_en.why: All render the closing formula idiomatically.

segments.sense: The smallest interval is a diesis. Next comes the semitone, whose rise is double that of a diesis, then the tone, made of two semitones and standing in the sesquioctave ratio 9:8. The semitone is as it were half of that ratio and the diesis as it were a quarter. If the interval is divided in exactly equal musical steps, the resulting ratios are (9/8)^(1/2) and (9/8)^(1/4), approximately 1.06066 and 1.02988.

errors.quote: and the diesis a quarter of it
errors.problem: The Latin repeats quasi for the diesis. The English allows the second subdivision to be read as unqualified.
errors.fix: and the diesis, as it were, a quarter of it

errors.quote: из двойного полутона / of a double semitone
errors.problem: The expression can suggest one recognized kind of semitone called a double semitone. The text uses ordinary doubling to give the composition of the tone.
errors.fix: из двух полутонов / of two semitones

errors.quote: neither is a ratio of whole numbers, hence the text's ‘quasi’
errors.problem: The arithmetic is correct if the musical interval is split into equal logarithmic steps. The specific causal claim about Xylander's quasi is not verified. The word qualifies the analogy to a half or a quarter, and the text never states this modern calculation.
errors.fix: Give the calculation conditionally and leave the force of quasi at ‘as it were’. Specify whole-number terms when contrasting Boethius's impossibility result with the subsequent geometric argument.

text_issues_review.printed: dimidium sesquioctauæ diesis autem (42.14)
text_issues_review.proposal: punctuate: dimidium sesquioctavae, diesis autem
text_issues_review.why: The scan has no stop after sesquioctavae. The conjunction autem and the second quasi introduce a separate coordinated proposition. A comma or stronger point would make the already recoverable grammar clear.
evidence: Lewis and Short, A Latin Dictionary, s.v. quasi I [checked]

best_ru.why: Preserves both occurrences of quasi and makes accessio intelligible in terms of pitch.

best_en.why: Clear scope for double and exact notation for the named ratio.

notes_to_keep.gist: Distinguish dividing the numerical excess linearly from dividing the interval into equal multiplicative steps. Boethius's worked example uses 16, 17 and 18. Boethius, De institutione musica I.16–17, ed. Friedlein (1867), pp. 201–204 [checked]
The rise is double in interval size, and both subdivisions are qualified by quasi.

editor_questions: Insert punctuation between the two quasi clauses in the reading text if the normalization permits it.

segments.sense: In arithmetic, the unit cannot be divided. A unit discerned in material magnitude can nonetheless be divided geometrically.

divergences.latin: ratione numeri unitas dividi non potest
divergences.issue: Does ratione numeri characterize the domain or make the unit a number?

readings.construal: The unit is indivisible under the rules of number.

quotes.ru: Ведь хотя с точки зрения числа единица делиться не может, всё же единица, усматриваемая в материи, делится геометрически.
quotes.en: For although in terms of number the unit cannot be divided, yet the unit that is seen in matter is divided geometrically.

quotes.ru: Ибо хотя с точки зрения числа единица не может быть разделена, однако единица, которая усматривается в материи, безусловно делится геометрически.
quotes.en: For although, by the reckoning of number, unity cannot be divided, yet unity that is seen in matter is certainly divided geometrically.

readings.construal: B in both languages and D in Russian describe the unit as a number. D English instead says ‘considered numerically’, which preserves the domain distinction.

quotes.ru: Ведь хотя единица как число неделима, единица, которую мы наблюдаем в материи, вполне допускает геометрическое деление.
quotes.en: For although unity cannot be divided as a number, unity as observed in matter can indeed be divided geometrically.

quotes.ru: Ведь хотя единица, если рассматривать её как число, не поддаётся делению, единицу, данную в материи, всё же можно разделить геометрически.
quotes.en: For although the unit cannot be divided when considered numerically, the unit as discerned in matter can certainly be divided geometrically.

divergences.verdict: Ratione numeri locates the statement within number or numerical reasoning. A/C and D English retain that distinction. B and D Russian are intelligible but risk implying that the unit is itself a number. Euclid expressly distinguishes a unit from a number, which is a multitude of units.
divergences.recommended_ru: Хотя в арифметическом счёте единица неделима, единицу, данную в материи, всё же можно разделить геометрически.
divergences.recommended_en: Although the unit is indivisible in arithmetic, the unit discerned in matter can nevertheless be divided geometrically.

best_ru.why: Distinguishes arithmetical reckoning from the material case without identifying the unit as a number.

best_en.why: The unit is the term used in the mathematical distinction.

notes_to_keep.gist: Explain the contrast between the unit that grounds counting and continuously divisible magnitude. Euclid, Elements VII, definitions 1–2 [checked].

segments.sense: The string corresponding to a sesquioctave ratio 9:8 can be divided to yield the semisesquioctave (the semitone), and that can again be divided to yield a diesis. Equal division of the tone would use the mean proportional of the two bounding lengths, such as √72 between 8 and 9.

best_ru.why: Clearly marks the two successive results and retains the ratio name.

best_en.why: Yield makes the division intelligible without taking the resulting interval for a physical string segment.

notes_to_keep.gist: Explain the geometric mean and distinguish a midpoint of string length from the point giving equal intervals. Euclid, Elements VI.13, Clark University edition [checked]

segments.sense: Geometry can always subtract the lesser straight length from the greater and add the greater to the lesser. A figure can accordingly be enlarged or diminished at will.

best_ru.why: Отрезок прямой correctly gives the finite straight magnitude under discussion.

best_en.why: Shorter and longer are exact in the geometrical setting, and each semper is kept.

notes_to_keep.gist: Euclid's construction of removing the equivalent of a lesser straight line from a greater supplies the mathematical parallel. Euclid, Elements I.3 [checked].

segments.sense: The geometrical freedom just described does not hold in arithmetic.

best_ru.why: Carries the argument forward naturally.

best_en.why: Gives the scope of id and the contrast signaled by vero.

segments.sense: Arithmetic cannot bisect a square number into two equal square numbers or double it and still have a square. Xylander illustrates this with sixteen, half of which is eight and double of which is thirty-two. Neither eight nor thirty-two is an integer square. Geometry can make both areas as squares. The transmitted Numerorum is syntactically awkward.

divergences.latin: Numerorum enim sedecim, qui est quadratus
divergences.issue: How should the irregular opening of the numerical example be construed?

readings.construal: Construes numerorum as a loose partitive, explicitly retained as among numbers.

quotes.ru: Кроме того, [арифметика] не может разделить предложенный квадрат на равные квадраты или построить вдвое больший. Ведь среди чисел шестнадцать, которое есть квадрат, она не может ни разложить на два квадрата (ибо арифметически невозможно, чтобы восемь было квадратом, и невозможно дать квадратный корень этого числа), ни дать другой квадрат, вдвое больший его (ибо не может быть, чтобы число тридцать два было квадратом). А для геометрии сделать это нетрудно.
quotes.en: Moreover, [arithmetic] cannot divide a given square into equal squares, or produce its double. For among numbers sixteen, which is a square, it can neither part into two squares (for it is impossible arithmetically for eight to be a square, or to give the square root of that number), nor can it give another square that is its double (for it cannot be that the number thirty-two is a square). But for geometry this is not hard to do.

readings.construal: Uses the intended numeral with an understood singular number rather than reproducing the loose genitive on its own.

quotes.ru: Кроме того, данный квадрат нельзя разделить на равные квадраты или получить из него квадрат вдвое больший. Ведь число шестнадцать — квадратное, но его нельзя ни разложить на два [равных] квадрата (в арифметике число восемь не может быть квадратом, и квадратный корень из него дать невозможно), ни удвоить так, чтобы получить другой квадрат (число тридцать два не может быть квадратным). В геометрии же сделать это нетрудно.
quotes.en: Moreover, a given square cannot be divided into equal squares or made into a square twice its size. For one cannot split the number sixteen, which is square, into two [equal] squares (in arithmetic eight cannot be a square, nor can a square root be given for that number), or double it to give another square (for thirty-two cannot be a square number). In geometry this is not difficult to do.

quotes.ru: Кроме того, [арифметика] не может ни разделить предложенный квадрат на равные квадраты, ни сделать его двойным. Ведь число шестнадцать, которое является квадратом, она не может ни разложить на два квадрата (ибо невозможно ни восьми быть арифметически квадратом, ни дать квадратный корень этого числа), ни дать другой квадрат, вдвое больший его (ибо не может быть, чтобы число тридцать два было квадратом). Геометрии же сделать это нетрудно.
quotes.en: Moreover, [arithmetic] cannot divide a proposed square into equal squares, or make it double. For it cannot split the number sixteen, which is a square, into two squares (for it is impossible for eight to be arithmetically a square, or to give the square root of that number), nor give another square double of it (for it cannot be that the number thirty-two is a square). But for geometry this is not difficult to do.

quotes.ru: Кроме того, арифметика не может ни разделить данный квадрат на равные квадраты, ни удвоить его. Таково, например, квадратное число шестнадцать. Арифметика не может ни разложить его на два квадрата (ведь невозможно, чтобы восемь было квадратом в арифметическом смысле или чтобы можно было указать квадратный корень этого числа), ни получить другой квадрат, удвоив шестнадцать (ведь число тридцать два не может быть квадратом). Геометрии же сделать это нетрудно.
quotes.en: Moreover, arithmetic cannot divide a given square into equal squares or double it. Take the number sixteen, which is a square. Arithmetic can neither resolve it into two squares (for eight cannot be a square in arithmetic, nor can one give a square root of that number) nor give its double as another square (for the number thirty-two cannot be a square). Geometry, however, finds no difficulty in doing this.

divergences.verdict: The singular relative leads to numerus as the implied term, and sixteen is what arithmetic tries to divide. A's construction makes the print's difficulty visible, but among numbers sixteen can sound like sixteen unspecified numbers. Translate the one numeral clearly and put the loose genitive and possible emendation in the commentary.
divergences.recommended_ru: Ведь число шестнадцать, будучи квадратным, нельзя разделить на два квадрата…
divergences.recommended_en: For arithmetic cannot divide sixteen, which is a square number, into two squares…

best_en.why: Makes the two operations and their restriction to arithmetic clear.

Sixteen has other equal-square partitions, for example four copies of four. The illustrated impossibility is specifically bisection into equal squares.

segments.sense: Taking the original side as the new diagonal gives a square of half the original area. Taking the original diagonal as the new side gives a square of twice the original area. For side s, the areas are s²/2 and 2s². The ending propositum dupli is irregular, though its result is fully determined by the construction.

divergences.issue: Is the result another square twice the original or the original square in a doubled size?

readings.construal: The new square is twice the original.

quotes.ru: Ибо стоит геометру, приняв сторону данного квадрата за диагональ, построить вокруг [неё] квадрат, как тот сразу оказывается половиной предложенного; и опять-таки, приняв диагональ данного квадрата за сторону, он начертит на ней квадрат, который, как известно, вдвое больше предложенного.
quotes.en: For the geometer, having taken the side of the given square in place of the diagonal, has only to set a square about [it], and that is at once the half of the one proposed; and again, taking the diagonal of the given square in place of the side, he will describe on it a square which is known to be the double of the one proposed.

quotes.ru: В самом деле, если геометр возьмёт сторону данного квадрата за диагональ и построит вокруг неё квадрат, то сразу получит половину данного квадрата. Если же он примет диагональ данного квадрата за сторону, то построит на ней квадрат, который, как ясно, вдвое больше данного.
quotes.en: For when a geometer takes the side of the given square as a diagonal and constructs a square around it, the new square is at once half the given one. Conversely, he will take the diagonal of the given square as a side and construct on it a square evidently twice the size of the original.

readings.construal: The new square is the original given in doubled size, preserving the surface cases through a genitive of measure.

quotes.ru: Ведь геометр, приняв сторону данного квадрата вместо диагонали, — едва он опишет вокруг [неё] квадрат, этот [квадрат] тотчас оказывается половиной предложенного; и опять, приняв диагональ данного квадрата вместо стороны, он опишет на ней квадрат, который, как известно, есть предложенный [квадрат] в двойном размере.
quotes.en: For the geometer, having taken the side of the given square in place of a diagonal, as soon as he has drawn a square around [it], that [square] is at once half of the proposed one; and again, having taken the diagonal of the given square in place of a side, he will describe a square on it, which, as is evident, is the proposed [square] of double [size].

readings.construal: The new square effects the envisaged doubling without explicitly stating the two terms of the comparison.

quotes.ru: В самом деле, если геометр возьмёт сторону данного квадрата за диагональ и опишет вокруг неё квадрат, то сразу получит половину исходного квадрата. Если же он, наоборот, примет диагональ данного квадрата за сторону, то опишет на ней квадрат и тем самым, очевидно, получит искомое удвоение.
quotes.en: For if the geometer takes the side of the given square as a diagonal and constructs a square about it, the result is at once half the original. If in turn he takes the diagonal of the given square as a side, he will draw on it a square which clearly gives the doubling proposed.

divergences.verdict: The intended mathematical comparison is beyond doubt: the square built on the original diagonal has twice the original area. The printed endings cannot easily give that comparative idiom. A and B are clearest about which square has which area. C usefully draws attention to the transmitted difficulty, but its wording can suggest the same square changes size.
divergences.recommended_ru: …квадрат, который, как ясно, вдвое больше данного.
divergences.recommended_en: …a square which is clearly twice the area of the original.
evidence: Allen and Greenough, New Latin Grammar §§345–346 [checked]
Euclid, Elements I.47, Clark University edition [checked]

segments.sense: These larger intervals are neither immediate nor incomposite, since they pass through the intervening intervals already described. Their character as intervals is defined by the sounding from first to last note. Their names derive from the notes traversed: four for the fourth, five for the fifth, and all eight for the octave. quotes.en: These, however, are neither immediate nor incomposite, but pass through all the aforesaid intervals as intermediate ones. And they are called intervals, indeed, with respect to the sound that there is from the first note to the last; but from the quantity of the intermediate notes they have found names of this kind: the fourth [‘through four’], because it passes through four notes or strings; the fifth [‘through five’], because through five; the octave [‘through all’], because through all, that is, through eight.

quotes.en: These intervals neither lack intermediate [steps] nor are they incomposite. They pass through all the intervening intervals mentioned above. They are called intervals in view of the sound from the first note to the last. They acquired their particular names from the number of intervening notes. The fourth [is called ‘through four’] because it passes through four notes or strings, the fifth because it passes through five, and the octave because it passes through all, that is, through eight.

The octave, the octave and a fourth, the octave and a fifth, and the double octave are consonant in the kind they call antiphony, meaning something like ‘sounding opposite’.

segments.sense: Paraphony is consonance at different times, with an even and smooth succession of notes in mutual proportions and ratios. The two accusatives in this description have no clear governor. Antiphony is simultaneous consonance of high and low, illustrated by four parallel pairs a seven-step octave apart.

quotes.ru: Между парафонным и антифонным, то есть «звучащим при» и «звучащим навстречу», разница та, что первое консонирует в неравное время, когда звуки, [храня] взаимные свои пропорциональности и отношения, с некоторой равномерностью мягко и складно сменяют друг друга. Антифонное же — это когда высокое консонирует с низким вместе, в одно и то же время: например, когда восьмой [звук] с первым, одиннадцатый с четвёртым, двенадцатый с пятым, пятнадцатый с восьмым равномерно восходит или нисходит в повышениях или понижениях, так что низкие [звуки] высоким, или наоборот, отвечают пропорционально.
quotes.en: Between the paraphonon and the antiphonon, that is, the ‘sounding to’ and the ‘sounding over against’, the difference is this: the former is consonant at unequal time, when the notes, [keeping] their mutual proportionalities and ratios, succeed one another gently and neatly with a certain evenness. The antiphonon, on the other hand, is when high is consonant with low together, at the same time: as when the eighth [note] rises or falls evenly with the first, the eleventh with the fourth, the twelfth with the fifth, the fifteenth with the eighth, in raisings or lowerings, so that low [notes] answer to high, or the reverse, proportionally.

readings.construal: Treat the accusatives as the respect in which the succession has evenness, broadly equivalent to an implicit ‘according to’ or ‘in’.

quotes.ru: Парафония и антифония, то есть созвучие вторящее и ответное, различаются следующим. При парафонии звуки консонируют в разное время, когда они плавно и стройно следуют друг за другом, соблюдая некоторую равномерность во взаимных пропорциях и отношениях. Антифония же бывает, когда высокий звук консонирует с низким одновременно, как при равном повышении или понижении восьмого звука с первым, одиннадцатого с четвёртым, двенадцатого с пятым, пятнадцатого с восьмым, так что низкие звуки пропорционально отвечают высоким или наоборот.
quotes.en: Paraphony and antiphony, that is, sounding in accompaniment and sounding in answer, differ as follows. In the former the notes are consonant at unequal times, succeeding one another smoothly and fittingly with a certain evenness in their mutual proportions and ratios. Antiphony occurs when a high note is consonant with a low one at the same time, as when the eighth and the first, the eleventh and the fourth, the twelfth and the fifth, and the fifteenth and the eighth rise or fall by equal changes in pitch, so that the low notes correspond proportionately to the high, or the reverse.

quotes.ru: Между парафонным и антифонным, то есть «призвучным» и «противозвучным», та разница, что первое консонирует в неодинаковое время, когда звуки по своим взаимным пропорциональностям и отношениям с некоторой равномерностью мягко и слаженно сменяют друг друга. Антифонное же — когда высокое консонирует с низким вместе, в одно и то же время: например, когда восьмой [звук] с первым, одиннадцатый с четвёртым, двенадцатый с пятым, пятнадцатый с восьмым одинаково поднимается или опускается в повышениях или понижениях, так что низкие пропорционально отвечают высоким или наоборот.
quotes.en: Between the paraphonon and the antiphonon, that is, the ‘sounding-to’ and the ‘sounding-against’, there is this difference: the former is consonant at unequal times, when the notes, in their mutual proportionalities and ratios, succeed one another gently and harmoniously with a certain evenness. The antiphonon is when the high is consonant with the low together, at the same time: as when the eighth [note] with the first, the eleventh with the fourth, the twelfth with the fifth, the fifteenth with the eighth rises or falls equally in raisings or lowerings, so that the low correspond proportionally to the high, or the reverse.

quotes.ru: Парафония и антифония, то есть «звучание в ответ» и «встречное звучание», различаются следующим образом. При первой звуки консонируют в разное время: соблюдая известную равномерность в своих взаимных пропорциях и отношениях, они плавно и стройно следуют друг за другом. Антифония же возникает, когда высокий звук консонирует с низким одновременно, в один и тот же миг. Так, при повышениях или понижениях восьмой звук поднимается или опускается наравне с первым, одиннадцатый — с четвёртым, двенадцатый — с пятым, пятнадцатый — с восьмым, и низкие звуки соразмерно отвечают высоким или наоборот.
quotes.en: Paraphony and antiphony, that is, ‘sounding in response’ and ‘sounding opposite’, differ in this respect. In the former the notes are consonant at different times, succeeding one another smoothly and harmoniously with a certain evenness in their mutual proportions and ratios. Antiphony occurs when a high note is consonant with a low one at the very same time. Thus in raisings or lowerings [of pitch] the eighth rises or falls equally with the first, the eleventh with the fourth, the twelfth with the fifth, and the fifteenth with the eighth, so that the low notes answer the high in due proportion, or conversely.

divergences.verdict: The print gives bare accusatives with no visible participle or preposition. Sibi already supplies the complement required by succedunt in its sense of succeeding. A respect construction or bracketed ‘keeping’ gives nearly the same relation, but ordinary accusative-of-specification examples are narrower, and a lacuna remains conjectural.
